one_line: Iranian strikes on Qatar's Ras Laffan Industrial City cut a large share of the world's helium supply, which chip fabs need.
summary: Strikes on Qatar's Ras Laffan gas hub in March 2026 cut a large share of the world's helium supply. Chip fabs use helium to cool and purge their tools, and news reports say fabs in South Korea drew down emergency stocks. On our map, the companies directly tied to helium so far are the gas companies: Air Products, which both buys crude helium and sells helium, so the effect on it could go either way, and Linde, which produces helium largely in the United States and may gain from higher prices. The map does not yet know which chipmakers buy helium, so the companies most likely to be hurt are not on this page yet.
title: Strikes knock out Qatar's Ras Laffan gas hub
